title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer during regional failover edge-case
author: Priya Raman
description:
Motivation: we observed a production incident where the SLO enforcer triggered aggressive load-shedding in Region-B during a cross-region failover while a small set of long-running in-flight requests were still being proxied. Root cause: the regional quorum check didn't account for in-flight token ownership and transient connection handovers, which caused the enforcer to consider capacity lower than it actually was and trip circuit-breakers too aggressively. This PR fixes the quorum and ordering race, adds hysteresis for short-lived fluctuations, and hardens the failover path to avoid duplicate shedding decisions.

Changes in this PR: adjust quorum calculation to include transient in-flight ownership, introduce 300ms hysteresis window on regional capacity transitions, add an ordering guard to prevent double-enqueue of the same request during handover, and add unit + integration tests that simulate cross-region proxy handoffs. Also includes a targeted canary config for rollout and a small metrics tag change to make incident triage easier.

Rollback plan: revert is a single commit revert; the change is guarded by a runtime feature flag (slo.enforcer.regional_quorum_v2) enabled by default for this hotfix but can be turned off immediately if issues appear.

Notes: marked as hotfix due to recent production impact (INC-2026-43). This PR was paired with a short-lived traffic migration (Regional B -> A) to validate behavior under load. CI initially failed due to a flaky integration test; test was stabilized by adding a mock time helper and retry assertion.

Related: ENG-3456, SUP-234

fix(slo-enforcer): prevent duplicate enqueue during proxy handover (ordering guard)

ops: add canary rollout config for hotfix
docs: release notes entry for hotfix
review_comments: Carlos Mendes: Can you explain why we chose 300ms for hysteresis? Is there experimental data?
Priya Raman: 300ms is based on tail-latency spikes observed in the last incident (p50-p99 delta ~180ms) plus conservative buffer; included rationale and benchmark notes in quorum_test.go comments.
Aisha Khan: Integration test looked flaky locally for me, what did you change?
Priya Raman: switched to mock time and added a retry/assert loop to tolerate scheduling noise; CI now passes consistently.
Jonah Li (approve): Verified logic and unit tests. Integration run on canary passed for a small traffic window.
release_notes: Hotfix: Stabilize SLO enforcer during regional failover by fixing quorum calculation, adding short hysteresis to capacity transitions, and preventing duplicate enqueue during proxy handover. Resolves incident INC-2026-43.
risk: low (targeted hotfix behind runtime flag, canary rollout enabled)
test_plan: Unit tests added and integration scenario simulating cross-region handoffs. Deployed to hotfix canary overlay for 2 hours under low traffic, then ramped to 10% for 30 minutes before full merge. Monitor slo.enforcer.metrics.{quorum,failures,load_shed} and rollback if failure rate increases.
notes: This patch is intentionally small: quorum and ordering guards are minimal diffs to reduce regression risk. Follow-up: consider generalizing hysteresis window as a tunable per-region metric and adding e2e chaos tests for long-lived in-flight requests.
